content: Hello, this is Jason from Amazon Security. I'm calling regarding some suspicious activity on your Amazon account. Are you the primary account holder?
Yes, I am. What kind of activity are you seeing?

Thank you for confirming. Our system detected several attempted purchases for electronics earlier today. For your protection, we've temporarily placed a hold on your account. Have you or anyone in your household tried to buy a gaming console or a tablet recently?
Oh no, my son has access to my Amazon account and he might have tried to order something without asking.
I understand, and don't worry, these things happen. Our goal is to ensure your account and funds are secure. May I have your full name and the best phone number to verify your profile?
Sure, it's Rebecca Turner. My phone number is 555-6321.

Thank you, Rebecca. I appreciate your cooperation. Before we proceed, I'll need to do a quick verification to confirm your account ownership. Could you please provide the email address linked to your Amazon account?
It's rebecca.t@email.com.
Perfect. I'm just cross-checking your details. While that's processing, can you confirm if any recent Amazon gift card purchases have appeared on your account statement?
I'm not sure. I haven't bought any gift cards myself, but I can check.

Thank you. The reason I ask is because unauthorized purchases often involve gift cards. If you see any charges you don't recognize, let me know. To restore access, we'll need to follow Amazon's secure verification protocol to ensure you're the rightful owner.
Okay, what do I need to do?
Amazon's protocol requires a secure verification step using gift card authentication. This is a temporary measure to protect your account. I'll walk you through each step, so there's no confusion.
Alright, but I just want to make sure my account is safe and I get any unauthorized money back.

Absolutely, Rebecca. Your security is our top priority, and this process will ensure no further unauthorized charges happen. First, please visit your nearest store and purchase three Amazon gift cards, each for $200. This is a refundable, temporary verification deposit.
So I just need to buy them at the store? Is this really standard?
Yes, this is Amazon's latest security measure for high-risk cases like yours. Once you provide the codes, the system will clear the fraudulent activity and refund the full amount to your account.
Okay, I'll head out to get the cards now. Do I need to keep the receipts?
Great question. Please keep both the gift cards and receipts, as they'll help us process your refund faster. When you're back, I'll guide you through the next step.
Alright, I'll call you when I'm back with the cards.
Thank you, Rebecca. I'll stay on the line in case you have any questions. Take your time.
Okay, I'm back and I have three $200 Amazon cards.
Excellent. Now, please read me the claim codes one at a time so I can enter them into the Amazon security portal for verification.
The first code is 8K4J-29LM-5XQ2.
Thank you. That code was accepted by the system. Please provide the second code.
The second one is 7R2D-6B8Y-LVQ9.
Perfect, that went through as well. And the third code?
The third code is 5F9G-Q2J6-MX7B.
All codes have been verified. The system confirms your account is now secure. You'll see a full refund of $600 to your Amazon balance within 24 hours.
Thank you. Is there anything else I need to do?

No further action is required. You did everything correctly and helped keep your account safe. If you notice any other unusual activity, call Amazon Security's main line directly. Have a great day, Rebecca.
Thank you for your help. I hope this doesn't happen again.
